critic_notes.rationale: The signs are internally consistent and the MIN "bottleneck" form is a genuine functional-form departure from a simple sum/product, but the economic content is very close to Ball et al.'s cash-based operating profitability, so it should be judged on whether the non-substitutability restriction adds anything beyond that known composite.

The expected negative sign contradicts the natural direction of the first factor (rising ROA is positively predictive via earnings momentum), and because the two ranks are multiplied without demeaning, high signal values are driven as much by profitability improvement as by accrual escalation, so the score cannot isolate the claimed interaction.

The second leg is essentially the textbook Sloan (1996) balance-sheet working-capital accrual measure (less depreciation) and the first is operating margin, making this a direct rediscovery of the accruals×profitability combination rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.

Adding a signed 3-period mean accrual to an always-positive 3-period accrual volatility before ranking is a scale-mismatched, arbitrarily weighted composite whose dominant term is unidentifiable, and the underlying idea (profitability × accrual quality/volatility) restates known cash-based profitability and accrual-quality results.

The conditional structure is coherent and correctly signed, and is the most genuinely novel construction in this batch, but roughly half the sample collapses to exactly zero, which pools cash-unconfirmed firms with the worst profitability improvers and will make the short leg and lower quintiles economically meaningless unless the gate is respecified as a two-sided contrast.

Compustat recch and invch are already stated as "decrease (increase)," so NEG(recch+invch) is high precisely when receivables and inventory are *accumulating* — the expression's direction is the opposite of the stated hypothesis and expected sign.

This is essentially the archived "Supplier-Independent Gross Profit" with the sparse apalch leg swapped for Δ(lct−dlc) and MUL swapped for MIN — the hypothesis text is nearly verbatim identical and the mechanism (Novy-Marx gross profitability × Sloan-style operating-liability accruals) is unchanged, so it reads as a coverage-driven cosmetic variant rather than a new economic idea.

Internally consistent and distinct from the archive, but the economic link is weak: Δ(che − dlc) is dominated by financing and investment policy (equity issuance, capex timing, payout) rather than by the cash realization of accrued earnings, so the "accrual-quality" interpretation is a stretch and the leg may mostly proxy for cash-holdings growth.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the book-tax/taxes-payable channel is a reasonably fresh accrual proxy, but txp is a small, lumpy, sparsely populated item and the indicator gate collapses all loss firms to exactly zero, creating a large mass point in the middle of the sort that will blur the long-short portfolio.

The core content is the well-published net-operating-assets / working-capital level anomaly (Hirshleifer et al.), and the only new element is a TS_RANK over a 3-period window that can take just three discrete values, giving an extremely coarse and noisy "recent peak" measure on top of an indicator that again piles loss firms at zero.

The invch sign convention is correctly reasoned and the expected negative sign matches the expression's natural direction, and conditioning inventory build-up on margin expansion is a genuine twist on the known inventory-growth anomaly — though the proposal ignores that invch-based legs delivered only ~6% coverage in the archive, which is the main threat to the portfolio test.

This is a plain profitability ratio with a rescaled denominator rather than a cross-theme interaction, it is close to standard profitability/ROA anomalies, and act−che can be near zero or tiny for asset-light firms, so the ranking will be driven by denominator noise that 1% winsorization only partly contains.

This is a mechanical recombination of two archive signals (the EBITDA-growth leg of "Debt-Funded EBITDA Improvement" times the negated change-in-net-liquid-assets leg of "Net-Liquid Profitability"), and because the rank leg is confined to [0,1] the signal's sign is entirely driven by the already-tested liquidity leg, so it largely re-runs the prior result with the sign flipped.

It reuses the same two ingredients as the archive's "Cash-Share-Verified Core Margin" but substituting persistent 3-period trends for a level and a one-period change is a defensible, motivated response to that signal's weak portfolio tails rather than a pure relabeling — though it remains a modest refinement rather than a new mechanism.

The expression correctly implements the stated realization cycle (prior-year working-capital build, current-year release, conditioned on profitability), the timing structure is genuinely distinct from the standard accruals level/change anomaly, and the profitability gate plausibly separates harvesting from distress-driven liquidation; the main risk is that a three-way MIN gate yields thin, unstable long tails.

The construction is internally consistent and the depreciation-quality channel is under-explored relative to accrual signals, but because Δ(oiadp/sale) mechanically contains −Δ(dpc/sale), the two legs are algebraically overlapping and any result will be hard to distinguish from a plain depreciation-intensity-change signal (itself close to the Abarbanell–Bushee fundamental signals).

With the profit-growth leg bounded in [0,1], the signal reduces to a positively-weighted receivables-accrual measure whose predicted negative sign is simply the Sloan/receivables accrual anomaly, and the label "conditional" misdescribes what is a signed multiplicative product with no gate.

A three-way MIN gate on profitability, R&D intensity, and an archive cash-share change leg is a kitchen-sink composite whose R&D-plus-profitability core rediscovers the established R&D-intensity/quality anomaly, while the economic link between R&D expensing and a one-year cash-share shift is asserted rather than argued, and the conjunction of high profitability with high R&D will leave a narrow, sector-concentrated long tail.

This is essentially a one-variable substitution inside the archive's strongest signal (che/act → (che−dlc)/act) that mechanically grafts on the already-tested Net-Liquid Profitability leg, so it is a cosmetic refinement with limited incremental information, and netting dlc also destroys the bounded "floor" interpretation the original relied on.

The second leg, NEG(Δwcap/lagged assets), is a direct restatement of the published working-capital accruals anomaly, and multiplying it by a profitability-change rank is the standard textbook "earnings quality" screen already partially covered by the archive's Working-Capital Harvest, so novelty is minimal.

The liquidity leg is a genuinely different construct from the archived cash/current-asset floor — cash coverage of non-debt (operating accrual) current liabilities, bounded and well-behaved — and the MIN bottleneck matches the stated "profit backed by settlement capacity" mechanism with consistent sign.

The expression computes what the hypothesis states, but subtracting dpc from oancf mostly loads on capital/depreciation intensity rather than cash-earnings quality, and pairing it with oiadp (already net of depreciation) double-penalizes the same item while sitting close to the published cash-based operating profitability result.

Applying 3-year moving averages to both legs of the archived Debt-Interest Timing Gap is a smoothing-parameter variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the averaged Δdlc term telescopes into multi-year debt growth, pulling the signal toward the known debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly.

Revenue-scaled noncash-current-asset intensity measured as a multi-year trend is a distinct construct from the archive's asset-scaled one-period accrual changes, the MIN bottleneck cleanly encodes "sustained margin requiring less accrual capital," and the sign direction is internally consistent.

This is a largely cosmetic recombination of the archive's "Cash-Share-Verified Core Margin" (identical DELTA(che/act,1) leg) with a lagged profitability rank and MIN instead of MUL, and lagging the profit leg only makes the signal staler without adding a distinct economic mechanism.

It replicates the structure of the already-successful "Cash-Covered Operating Profit" with a much narrower and lumpier denominator, and che/(che+txp) saturates near 1 for the large fraction of firms with negligible taxes payable, so the second leg will be near-degenerate noise rather than a real tax-settlement-capacity measure.

The level-based reformulation of the debt-interest gap is a defensible substantive departure from the archive's change-based version with internally consistent signs, though the gap is likely dominated by debt-maturity mix and credit quality (cheap debt, low rates) rather than any concealed financing burden.

The "new historical low in noncash-working-capital intensity" leg is a genuinely different functional form from the archive's trend version and the construction matches the stated hypothesis, but it remains a within-family refinement whose incremental information over the existing trend signal may be small.

Internally consistent and pairs a distinct profit source (SG&A intensity change) with a cash-coverage change rather than re-using the same profitability leg, though it is a change-on-change double sort that will be noisy and thematically close to the archive's cash-verification cluster.

The second leg is essentially a monotone transform of net non-cash working capital scaled to (0,1), so the signal largely rediscovers the well-known net-operating-assets/working-capital accrual anomaly, and its stated direction directly contradicts the archive's own "Supplier-Independent Gross Profit" premise that heavier reliance on operating liabilities degrades profit quality.

This is a mechanical crossbreed of two archive winners — the MA(oibdp/at) × coverage-ratio structure of "Cash-Covered Operating Profit" with the TS_MIN operator already used in "Persistent Cash-Floor Profitability" — so it is a cosmetic timing variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

Moving from the already-tested trend/breakout formulations to a level ceiling is a defensible construction change, but NEG(TS_MAX(noncash current assets/revenue)) is largely a smoothed operating-asset-level signal and thus leans on the well-documented net-operating-assets/working-capital anomaly, limiting its incremental novelty.

The expression is internally coherent and the positive-part operator is economically sensible, but it is a narrow asymmetry tweak to the archive's "Debt-Interest Timing Gap" (and closely overlaps "Profitable Debt-Interest State Gap"), so it reads as a refinement of an already-measured effect rather than a new test.

The recch sign convention, the at-scaling of both receivables and revenue changes, and the MIN long-leg construction are all internally consistent, and reframing the archive's tail-driven conditional short signal into a two-condition quality gate is a genuine structural change motivated by the earlier fmb/alpha disagreement.

Using aoloch as a bounded, sign-agnostic measure of unclassified accrual reliance is a genuinely new channel not present in the archive, though the denominator makes the ratio mechanically high for firms with near-zero operating cash flow, so low coverage and a cash-flow-magnitude confound should be diagnosed.

This is a single-leg monotone blend of gross profitability (Novy-Marx) and working-capital accruals (Sloan) with no genuine interaction structure, it duplicates the archive's "Accrual-Investment-Covered Profit" logic with core profit swapped for oancf, and the bounded ratio behaves erratically for loss-making firms where the numerator flips sign.

This is a leg-swap recombination of two archive signals — the cash-to-operating-claims coverage ratio from "Cash-Covered Operating Profit" and the one-year core-margin delta from "Collection-Confirmed Margin Expansion" — and the archive already shows that replacing the persistent-profitability level with a noisy margin change weakens both the FMB and alpha evidence, so it is a cosmetic rather than substantive refinement.

The construction is internally coherent (high score = prior noncash-current-asset buildup plus subsequent profit deterioration, expected negative) and the asymmetric-failure framing is a defensible non-mirror-image follow-up to the weak "Accrual-Investment Payoff," though it sits close to the classic working-capital accrual anomaly and the MIN of two moderately correlated legs may just re-express lagged accruals.

This is the fourth denominator variant of the same "MIN(persistent profitability, bounded cash-coverage ratio)" template already tested with che/(che+lct−dlc), oancf/(|oancf|+|dlc|), and oancf/(|oancf|+ΔNCA), and because oancf and oibdp are strongly correlated the second leg largely collapses into inverse operating-liability intensity, making it an incremental reshuffle rather than a new mechanism.

It is a direct level-to-trend substitution on "Depreciation-Stress-Tested Profit" with the identical second leg (TS_RANK(dpc/at,5)), i.e., precisely the kind of one-operator cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

Beyond being the constructed mirror of the already-tested "Accrual-Capital Efficiency Breakout," the INDICATOR gate zeroes out the majority of the cross-section and leaves a signal with a large point mass at zero — the exact design that produced near-null FMB t-stats for every conditional proposal in this archive.

The re-specification (asset-scaled change in |aoloch| rather than a ratio to near-zero operating cash flow) is a genuine diagnostic fix with a consistent expected sign, though the MUL of a [0,1] rank with a signed z-score means low-profitability firms are compressed toward zero and the raw |aoloch| change is likely very noisy.

This is essentially a merger of two already-tested archive winners (Cash-Covered Operating Profit and Cash-Covered Financing Claims) with the same oibdp leg, and the MAX(...,0) floor creates a large mass of firms with an identical zero residual whose tied ranks will dominate the MIN, making it a cosmetic denominator recombination with a degenerate construction rather than a new mechanism.

This is the archive's Failed Accrual Investment with MIN swapped for MUL and identical legs — precisely the kind of cosmetic aggregator variant the objective warns against, and it does not diagnose why the FMB slope was zero beyond asserting tail-specificity.

Both legs already appear in the archive, but pairing the persistent-margin level with the abnormal-receivables filter is an untested and economically coherent interaction; the main risks are the heavily reused MA(core margin,3) leg dominating results and the low (~0.06) coverage inherited from recch.

It is a one-leg swap of the gen-6 Inventory-Confirmed Gross-Margin Expansion signal, and the stated fix does not work — a MIN still selects firms with the most extreme inventory liquidation conditional on high margins, so the distress-liquidation contamination that produced the negative alpha remains.

This is close to a sign-flipped restatement of the archive's Debt-Funded EBITDA Improvement (profitability change × short-term-debt change), with only cosmetic substitutions (pi for ebitda, dlc/lct for dlc/at), so it is unlikely to deliver independent information.

It bolts the Depreciation-Reconciled leg — which produced a wrong-signed, insignificant alpha on its own — onto the existing Depreciation-Stress-Tested Profit signal, and since |dp − dpc| is near zero for most firms the added leg contributes mostly ties and thinner top buckets rather than incremental information.

The construction is scale-inconsistent — a single z-score of profit change is differenced against a two-z-score composite with roughly √2 the dispersion, so the "payoff spread" will be dominated by the lagged excess-accrual term and largely reproduces the archived excess-accrual-investment effect in linear form rather than testing a genuine payoff comparison.

The two coverage ratios are both monotone transforms of cash relative to a liability class and share `che` in numerator and denominator, so they are highly collinear; the MIN adds little beyond the already-archived Cash-Covered Financing Claims (alpha 0.044, t=4.58) and amounts to a mechanical restacking of two prior winners.

The intersection of two economically distinct archived components (own-history depreciation intensity and financing-claim cash coverage) with pretax profitability is coherent and the sign direction is internally consistent, though TS_RANK(dpc/at) may proxy for recent impairments or capex cycles rather than a clean capital-consumption stress test, and the value-add over the parents is incremental.

This is a triple-MIN stack of two already-accepted archived signals whose second and third legs are mechanically entangled (che/act and (act−che)/revt both hinge on the cash share of current assets), so the incremental information is likely small and any gain risks coming from narrower, less stable intersection membership.

The economics (new short-term financing funding accrual-bearing operating assets before interest hits earnings) are coherent and the expected negative sign matches the MIN's natural direction, but with a negative-sign weakest-link construction only the short leg is economically identified while the long leg pools firms failing any one of three unrelated conditions.

The absolute-value penalty symmetrically punishes large negative operating working capital, which is typically a sign of strong customer/supplier financing and is empirically associated with outperformance, so the stated mechanism partly contradicts the direction of the underlying evidence and the signal closely echoes the weak-performing archived Balanced Operating-Accrual Margin.

This is essentially the archived "Fully Burdened Pretax Profit" with a three-period moving average bolted on — and simultaneously the intersection of the already-tested "Cash-Covered Financing Claims" with the depreciation-rank leg — so it is a cosmetic smoothing variant rather than a new mechanism.

The archive already contains "Cash-Covered Operating Profit" with the identical cash-coverage leg and a nearly identical persistent-profitability leg; swapping oibdp→oiadp and MA→TS_MIN is a minor parameterization change, and the TS_MIN-floor device was already exercised in "Persistent Cash-Floor Profitability."

It is a splice of two archived designs (the accrual-capital breakout and the net operating-funding burden), but the shift from gross noncash current assets to a signed net funding requirement is an economically meaningful change that fixes a genuine defect (penalizing favorable supplier/customer financing), and the expression matches the stated hypothesis and sign.

This merely substitutes gross-profit growth for the operating-profit growth term in the archived "Standardized Accrual-Investment Payoff" while leaving the entire lagged excess-investment leg and standardization untouched; since oibdp is essentially revt−cogs−xsga, the payoff terms are highly collinear and the test is close to a rerun.

The components are all recycled from prior signals, but replacing a fragile three-way minimum with a ranked two-channel quality composite is a defensible aggregation change motivated by an actual portfolio-construction diagnosis, and the expression is internally consistent with a positive sign.

The construction is coherent and the negative sign follows naturally from the expression, and while it clearly extends the archived "Debt-Interest Timing Gap," adding a second adverse-funding channel via SUMRANK after the weakest-link version failed is a substantive rather than cosmetic revision — though the nonnegative IND_RANK multiplier means low-profitability firms are compressed toward zero and will muddle the short leg.
